title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1973-12-02
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: Warm, dark‑mellow ’73 show with a superb Weather Report Suite and half‑step jams, captured on a clear audience recording.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the mellow first set, Keith’s tasteful piano work, and a “weird but working” second set highlighted by Wharf Rat > Half‑Step > Playin' and an inspired jam that blends “Can’t You See” with Mind Left Body. The audience tape is praised for its warm ambience and good instrument separation, making the performance highly enjoyable despite some complaints about the release’s editing.

ai_rating.rationale: 13 reviews overwhelmingly give 5‑star praise for both music and sound; only one low rating concerns packaging, not performance, yielding an average above 4.5.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape noted for warm, dark ambience and clear separation of instruments (especially Keith and Bob). No major distortion or drop‑outs reported; a few listeners miss additional audience bleed.

standout_songs: "Can't You See"/Mind Left Body jam after Playin'
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as warm and mellow with strong piano work; second set is unconventional but cohesive, delivering deep psychedelic jams that keep the momentum flowing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Briefly noted for riffing “Can’t You See” during the Playin' jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as ‘battling giant dinosaurs’ on Half‑Step before resolving into a beautiful jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for interplay with Keith and highlighted in the post‑Playin' jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano work singled out as “nice things” on the first set; excellent separation from Bob noted.
